The real-time PCR approach has shown promising results in biomolecular identification of allergenic pollen. This method involves analyzing pollen mixes for specific allergens and can provide accurate quantification. Future perspectives suggest developing multiplex real-time PCR techniques for simultaneous detection of different taxa, which could enhance accuracy and speed up monitoring efforts.

Additionally, innovative high-throughput molecular methods are being explored to improve the detection of allergens in pollen samples. This new approach may lead to better aerobiological monitoring, enabling more effective management of allergies and protecting individuals from potential health risks associated with exposure to specific allergenic pollen species.

While more research is needed to fully establish the effectiveness of these methods, existing evidence suggests that biomolecular identification of allergenic pollen can be a valuable tool for aerobiological monitoring.
